newsitem.title: UK: Anglian Water to take over Hartlepool.
newsitem.headline: Anglian Water to take over Hartlepool.

text.p: British water company Hartlepool Water Plc said on Wednesday it had agreed to a takeover offer from bigger water firm Anglian Water which values Hartlepool at about 19.5 million pounds ($31.8 million).
Hartlepool said Anglian was paying 266 pence cash for each share in the target firm with a loan note alternative.

Anglian, which turned in pretax profits before exceptionals for the year of 257 million pounds ($419.2 million), up from 238.6 million, will offer price cuts of five percent to Hartlepool customers from April 2001.

Anglian paid out a total dividend of 34.5 pence per share, up from 30 pence, while Hartlepool shareholders will retain the final dividend of five pence per share to be paid on July 1, the statement said.
Anglian, which is one of Britain's large water and sewerage firms, said the deal enhanced its strategy of targetting "inset" appointments, where companies can compete to supply large customers.

Anglian also said it expected savings of 10 million pounds a year from a 20 million pound restructuring and said it believed that if it were impacted by proposals from the government to levy a one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, the revenue should be "committed to the benefit of the communities we serve." ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
